Read this first

  1. These are claims, not our measurements. Each publisher ran its own test. A lower KLD on one card is not evidence of a better file than a higher KLD on another.
  2. Methods rarely match. Publishers use different reference models (BF16, their own Q8_0, someone else's Q8_0), different text, context lengths and tools. Each row shows its reference; the cards below give the rest.
  3. Sizes mean different things. This model carries a 51B-parameter n-gram table that some files keep on disk. A size marked "GPU weights" or "resident" leaves it out. GiB figures are converted to GB.

Compare quants inside one measurement

Every point in a set was measured the same way by the same party, so points in one set can be compared with each other; points from different sets cannot. Your ticks carry across sets, so you can follow a quant through every set that measured it. Quants that publish no comparable numbers are listed under Repos without extracted claims.

Quants

When one publisher measured several

These are the only tables where different publishers' files went through the same test. They are still one party's measurement, often of competitors.

Same file, different numbers

Where two cards report on the same file, the figures rarely agree. The Setup column lists what each card states about its method; where the stated setups differ, that may explain the gap, but the cause of any particular difference is not established, and the two cards may not have tested the same file revision.

Publisher notes

Method, evaluation setup and problems we found, per repository. Line numbers refer to the card snapshot linked at the bottom of each note.

6block/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF

GGUF llama.cpp vs BF16

imatrix-calibrated tiers from BF16; protected tensors (router/SSM/HC F32, shared expert Q8_0, token_embd/output Q6_K, PLE table Q4_0); low tiers 'layered' (PLE Q4_0, savings spent on expert gate/up)

Reference
BF16 master (own run)
Eval data
wikitext-2 test, 12 chunks
Context
512
Tool
not stated (perplexity)
  • Tiny eval: 12 chunks x 512 tokens of wikitext-2 [L90]
  • Publisher says numbers are only comparable within this table [L91-92]
  • Claims layered tiers improve PPL ~14% vs the uniform tier at smaller size, but no uniform IQ2_XS/IQ1_M rows are shown [L52-53, L94-96]
  • Claim that PLE Q8_0 → Q4_0 'costs nothing' is stated without numbers [L50-51]
  • BF16 reference PPL 1.7164 on wikitext-2 is unusually low; other cards in this set report this architecture memorises wikitext via the n-gram table

How this was built

We listed every repository Hugging Face tags as a quantization of Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (453 on 2026-10-17) and saved each raw README.md at its pinned commit into a local ledger, so nothing is re-fetched. Cards that reproduce another publisher's numbers are detected by comparing claim lines across all cards and are not counted as independent measurements. Results published only as chart images were transcribed from their labels and checked against the marker positions in the image. Numbers were extracted with the line they came from, then a script confirmed that 3506 published values appear verbatim on their cited lines (0 failures). For every card that carried measured claims at the first pass (196 of 453), a second reader re-extracted the numbers without seeing our data, and disagreements were resolved against the source text; the remaining cards were each read in full by one reader. Rows a card quotes from elsewhere are marked "quoted" and are not counted as measurements; rows measured on a different model are left out (7). File sizes without a card figure come from Hugging Face's file listing at the same commit.

Not covered: claims made only off-site (other than Unsloth's docs page) or in images other than turboderp's, and repos created or changed after 2026-10-17. Found an error or a new quant? Open an issue or pull request; each claim lives in a plain data file with its source line.

QFF (Quant Fidelity Frontier): what publishers claim, pinned to the line they said it · data captured 2026-10-17 · claims belong to their publishers · source and data
